findings.what: aRUNCountLargerThanTheObjectIsRefusedToo is the round-2 segment-count defect, un-fixed one field over. It has the huge-overclaim fixture (0x7FFFFFFF) but no MODEST-overclaim companion, so it constrains 'an absurd count is refused' and not 'a count exceeding the bytes left is refused' -- exactly the distinction aSegmentCountOnlyMODESTLYTooLargeIsAlsoRefused was added to buy for the other repeat count. MEASURED SURVIVING MUTATION: in CommitDelta.readSegment, `runCount > c.remaining()` -> `runCount > Integer.MAX_VALUE / 2` (a fixed sanity cap -- the exact wrong refactor the remaining()-derived bound is chosen over). `./gradlew :format:test :ingest:test :sequencer:test` = BUILD SUCCESSFUL. The identical mutation on the segment count (`count > c.remaining()` -> `count > Integer.MAX_VALUE / 2`) IS killed, by aSegmentCountOnlyMODESTLYTooLargeIsAlsoRefused. The asymmetry is the finding: the same one-fixture fix works here (a v0 delta whose run count is, say, 9 with 8 trailing bytes, asserting on the '9 runs' message rather than merely 'runs').
findings.failure_scenario: A later refactor replaces the remaining()-derived run bound with a constant cap -- the natural thing to write when someone asks 'how many runs is too many?'. Every test stays green. A truncated PUT or a foreign writer then leaves a v0 delta -- the shape every bucket already holds, reachable from CommitLog.recover on the ordinary recovery path -- whose run count is 200,000,000. PROBED under the mutant on a 20-byte object: `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` out of ChainEntry.decode, past recover's own `throws IOException` and every caller catching it. That is the precise defect this commit widened scope to close, and the test the author added for it does not hold it closed.

findings.what: Neither repeat-count guard is constrained in its NEGATIVE half, on either count. Cursor.uvarint permits shift up to 63, so a crafted 10-byte varint yields a negative long. MEASURED SURVIVING MUTATIONS, both BUILD SUCCESSFUL across format+ingest+sequencer: (a) readSegment `runCount < 0 || runCount > c.remaining()` -> `runCount > c.remaining()`; (b) decodeBatchedBody `count <= 0` -> `count == 0` (the '0 segments' test uses only the literal zero). Production is correct in both places; nothing pins it.
findings.failure_scenario: A corrupt or hostile chain object encodes its run count as the 10-byte varint 0xFFFFFFFF80000000. PROBED under mutation (a): `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Illegal Capacity: -2147483648` escapes ChainEntry.decode as an UNCHECKED exception, past recover's `throws IOException` -- the same contract escape the guards' own comments name as their reason for existing, differing from the OOM only in which unchecked type gets out. A caller that catches IOException to skip a torn entry instead dies.
